title: Chicken Enchiladas
subtitle: rolled chicken tortillas baked in chipotle sauce
excerpt: Shredded chicken and soured cream rolled inside flour tortillas, covered in a smoky chipotle tomato sauce and melted cheese. This is a satisfying baked dish that comes together with simple ingredients.
sourceNotes: Enchiladas have been eaten in Mexico since the Aztec period. The modern baked version with cheese and cream sauce is more associated with the northern regions and Mexican-American cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze assembled but unbaked. Bake from frozen adding 15 extra minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and bake in two trays.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the day before and refrigerate. Bake just before serving.

content.text: Poach the chicken directly in the sauce to keep it moist. Once cooked, shred it with two forks and mix with soured cream. Roll the tortillas tightly so they hold their shape in the baking dish.

items.prepNote: use 1 chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, chopped

content.text: Cook the onion and garlic in a little oil in a large pan for 5 minutes. Add the cumin, smoked paprika, and tinned tomatoes. Stir well.
Add the chicken thighs to the sauce. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until cooked through.
Remove the chicken. Shred with two forks. Mix with the soured cream and season.
Preheat oven to 190C (fan 170C / gas 5). Spread a layer of sauce in the base of a baking dish.
Spoon chicken filling into each tortilla. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the dish.
Pour the remaining sauce over the tortillas. Scatter grated cheese on top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the cheese is golden and bubbling.

items.fix: Use less filling and roll firmly. Make sure they are placed seam-side down in the dish.

items.symptom: Cheese topping burnt before filling heated through
items.cause: Oven too hot or dish too shallow
items.fix: Cover with foil for the first 15 minutes and remove it to brown the cheese at the end.

items.cause: Chicken overcooked or not enough soured cream
items.fix: Keep the poaching at a gentle simmer. Add more soured cream to the shredded chicken before filling.

content.text: Enchiladas appear in Mexican cooking as far back as the Aztec period, when tortillas were dipped in chilli sauce. The modern baked version with cheese is more associated with northern Mexican cooking and the wider Mexican-American food tradition. They are one of the most popular Mexican dishes eaten outside Mexico. Every family has their own version.
